newsitem.title: USA: Pace of U.S. soyoil sales enthuses exporters.
newsitem.headline: Pace of U.S. soyoil sales enthuses exporters.

text.p: Indications that China and Morocco were buyers of U.S. soyoil in recent days generated more enthusiasm among U.S. exporters about the near-term health of that market.

"Demand for the U.S. product recently has been a real pleasant surprise," said one soyoil trader for a major commercial company. "It's been a positive development, and the question now is where do we go from here."
After a long dormancy, the soyoil export market has shown signs of life, and the solid pace of business was expected to continue, at least temporarily, U.S. exporters said.
Last week, the U.S. Department of Agriculture put total 1996-97 soyoil sales at 152,000 tonnes as of Oct. 31, versus 117,600 for the same period last year.
Morocco announced a tender for 66,000 tonnes of vegetable oil for February-April shipment, and was said to have already purchased 43,500 tonnes, one U.S. soyoil exporter said.
"Regarding Morocco, I can say it's true," another exporter said. "They did it (made the purchase) over the weekend."
Prices for the sale were unavailable, but the shipment was said to be for December, the exporter said.

The soyoil market also had China rumors to contend with on Wednesday. There was talk in CBOT and export markets that China bought 30,000 tonnes of U.S. soyoil for prompt shipment, but U.S. exporters could not confirm the business.
However, one cash market trader said freight on a 35,000 ton vessel at the U.S. Gulf had been fixed, and the ship was set for loading in the next several days.
"The word is that they're loading (soy) oil," the source said.
Futures responded to the export talk with lackluster action. As of 1230 CST, December soyoil was down 0.04 cent per pound at 23.00, and January was down 0.04 cent at 23.23.
